Implemented bounded, independent four-column GMRES batching.

  • Pair translations now serve all active columns in a batch.
  • Each column preserves its own Krylov basis, restarts, iteration budget and true-residual certificate.
  • Forward and adjoint solves use the same batching.
  • Scalar GMRES delegates to the shared implementation.

Seven focused Rust tests passed, including dense/physical/gradient comparisons, mixed scales and zeros, per-column iteration limits, and thread-count determinism. Python regressions were added and linted; execution awaits your rebuilt extension. Independent review found no correctness issues.

Changed: linalg/gmres.rs, its export, cluster/iterative.rs, and tests/tmatrix/test_iterative.py. No timing claim yet; edits remain frozen for your screen.

  • Batch cap increased from 4 to 8.
  • Singleton active columns now lend their existing vector directly, avoiding packing copies.
  • Single-column results move out their existing answer buffer.
  • One shared Arnoldi implementation remains.

items.html:
Ready and frozen; 35 focused Rust tests pass.

Changes since stage 2:

  • linalg/gmres.rs: allocate Krylov workspace only for columns requiring iterations.
  • cluster/iterative.rs: stronger eleven-column, near-touching sphere regression covering restarts, dense comparisons and gradient identities.
  • sw/plan.rs: outgoing forward translations use value-only Hankel sequences, avoiding unused derivatives and an extra radial order.

Finite forward values can now succeed where unused derivatives previously overflowed; actual radial overflow still errors. Regression coverage verifies both.

For further single-RHS gains, test Hankel recurrence plus this value-only change first. Direct translation action has modest, uncertain upside; sharing A/B contractions across helicities is more promising at higher multipole orders but requires greater specialization. No further edits or active jobs.
